A01_broken_access_control.notes: No access-control logic lives in the frontend. The store sends the trigger array as-is to the backend; the backend enforces projectId-scoped authorization. No client-side gating of save/delete that could be bypassed.

A02_cryptographic_failures.notes: No secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials appear in any changed file. The frontend bundle carries only UI strings.

A03_injection_xss.notes: No v-html or innerHTML usage in any changed file. All user-supplied data (triggerValue, eventName, keywords, entryStepId) is rendered via Vue {{ }} text interpolation or bound to native inputs with v-model — both paths auto-escape. The deep-link URL (t.me/...) is displayed in a {{ link }} text node (not an ), so no javascript: URI injection path exists. i18n step-type keys are rendered via t() which returns plain text. SearchableSelect option labels are text-interpolated (confirmed no v-html in its template).

A03_injection_client_side_logic.notes: The client-side duplicate-event-name guard is explicitly advisory (does not block save). The server 422 is the enforced backstop. No security logic has been moved client-only.

A04_insecure_design.notes: The trigger array is a full-replace payload sent to PATCH. Per-trigger and cross-trigger validation (duplicate event_name, dangling entryStepId, at-most-one on_start, event-only mid-entry) is handled server-side per tech-spec Decision 13/14. Client-side guards are advisory UX only.

A05_security_misconfiguration.notes: No new Nuxt config, CORS, or security-header changes in this diff. Unchanged from baseline.

A06_vulnerable_components.notes: No new npm dependencies introduced (user-spec constraint respected). Only Vue/Nuxt primitives reused.

A07_authentication_failures.notes: Frontend makes no authentication decisions. useApi() handles auth headers transparently. No new unauthenticated endpoints introduced.

A08_software_integrity.notes: No eval(), dynamic import with user data, or deserialisation of untrusted data. The trigger array flows through typed interfaces to the backend.

A09_logging_monitoring.notes: Frontend scope — no server-side logging surface. No console.log of sensitive data observed.

A10_ssrf.notes: No server-side requests constructed from user input. The deep-link URL is assembled client-side for clipboard copy only (t.me/<botUsername>?start=<triggerValue>); triggerValue is validated against /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,64}$/ before the link is shown; botUsername originates from the server (not user-typed). Link is displayed as text — never used as a fetch/redirect target.

url_deep_link_safety.notes: The link computed in FunnelTriggerSettings is suppressed when valueError is non-null (pattern guard). The link is rendered as text in a <code> element, not as a clickable <a :href>. No open-redirect or javascript: URI injection vector.

secrets_in_bundle.notes: Reviewed types/funnel.ts, stores/funnels.ts, FunnelTriggersPanel.vue, FunnelTriggerSettings.vue. No hardcoded secrets, API keys, tokens, or credentials.

input_rendering.notes: trigger.triggerValue is rendered as {{ tr.triggerValue || t(...) }} in the row header — text-only. Entry step labels use t(`funnels.steps.type.${s.stepType}`) where stepType is a controlled server enum with plain-text locale values. No HTML injection path.

mass_assignment.notes: FunnelTrigger interface carries only (triggerType, triggerValue, keywords, entryStepId) — exactly the backend TriggerDto contract. The store's update() sends payload verbatim; no extra fields are injected client-side.

notes: Audit scope: types/funnel.ts, stores/funnels.ts, FunnelTriggersPanel.vue (new), FunnelTriggerSettings.vue, FunnelStepForm.vue (keyboard scan patch), en.json, uk.json. Backend-side security (anti-IDOR CAS, projectId discipline, 422 validation, PII-free WARN logs) is out of scope for this frontend-only task. All frontend-relevant OWASP A01–A10 checks pass. Vue auto-escaping and the absence of v-html/innerHTML are the primary XSS safeguards; both are confirmed.
